watch-key.context: A small winding key with a rounded bow on top and a square barrel below. People use it for antique clock and pocket watch topics, repair and collecting.

watch-chain.context: A pocket watch chain with a ring at the top, a T bar across the middle and a diamond shaped fob hanging below. It stands for pocket watches, vintage fashion and waistcoat accessories.

draw-plate.context: A flat steel plate with a row of holes that get smaller from left to right. It is used for drawing wire to a thinner gauge in jewelry making and metalwork.

dapping-block.context: A metal block with round cavities of different sizes and a ball ended punch beside it. Jewelers use the set to shape flat metal discs into domes.

diamond-tester.context: A pen shaped electronic tester with a pointed metal probe and a row of indicator lights. Jewelers and buyers use it to check whether a stone is a real diamond.

carat-scale.context: A small digital scale with a weighing pan that holds a cut gem and a display window on the front. It is used to weigh gemstones in carats.

ingot-mold.context: A steel mold with a flared trough and short feet, with a bar shaped cavity inside. It is used to cast melted gold or silver into ingots.

casting-flask.context: A short metal cylinder drawn with a wax tree of branches inside, standing on a central sprue. It is used in lost wax casting to make several pieces of jewelry at once.

chasing-hammer.context: A hammer with a flat round face on one side, a ball peen on the other and a slim handle. Metalsmiths use it for chasing and repousse work and for shaping sheet metal.

graver.context: An engraving tool with a bulb shaped wooden handle and a short steel blade cut at an angle to a point. Engravers use it to cut lines and patterns into metal.

jewelers-bench.context: A workbench top seen from above with a half moon cutout at the front edge and a small catch tray underneath. It stands for a goldsmith or jewelry repair workshop.

wire-jig.context: A square pegboard with four pegs and a wire bent in a zigzag around them. Makers use it to bend identical wire links, clasps and shapes.

gem-scoop.context: A small scoop with a short handle holding a few loose cut stones above its bowl. It is used to pick up, sort and pour loose gemstones.

lunula-collar.context: A flat crescent shaped collar with a thick middle, narrower paddle ends and a dot of decoration. It stands for ancient gold neck ornaments from the Bronze Age.

touchstone.context: A dark stone tablet with bright streaks rubbed across it and a small gold bar touching it above. It is the classic way to judge the purity of gold by the colour of its streak.

gem-certificate.context: A certificate sheet with a cut gem at the top, lines of text and a round seal at the bottom. It stands for a gem grading report or an appraisal for a stone or piece of jewelry.

diamond-parcel.context: A folded paper packet shown flat with its creases and a small diamond in the middle. Dealers use these papers to carry and trade loose diamonds.

jewelry-pouch.context: A soft drawstring pouch with flared gathers at the top and a small ring peeking out of the opening. It stands for gift packaging and for storing or carrying jewelry.

jewelry-tag.context: A small price tag shaped like a house with a punched hole and a string loop looped over the top. Shops attach it to rings, necklaces and bracelets to show price and product details.

ring-resizing.context: A ring band with a cut gap at the bottom and two arrows pointing outward from the gap. It means making a ring larger, or cutting and soldering it to change its size.

cloisonne-enamel.context: A round plaque with four petal shaped cells outlined by raised wire. It stands for cloisonne, where coloured enamel is fired into wire compartments.

filigree.context: A round openwork pendant with four curling wire scrolls and a small dot at the centre. It stands for filigree, the lacy jewelry technique made from fine twisted wire.

casting-grain.context: A small triangular heap of round metal pellets resting on a flat base. It stands for casting grain or shot, the small metal beads used when alloying and melting precious metals.
